conflict: none — did not build, stage, or assemble
choice_reason: 1. A's confirm/detail dialogs use real ARIA modal semantics (role="dialog"/"alertdialog" with aria-modal="true") and an explicit keyboard focus trap (Tab cycles between first/last focusable elements, per A/source/app.js); B's dialogs use role="dialog" with no aria-modal and the source shows no evidence of a focus trap (a single el.focus() call in the whole file) — a real risk on a screen dedicated to destructive actions. 2. A's default view gives an immediate summary-tile overview (Needs review/Expired/Expiring/Active/Disabled counts) and a Production/Sandbox/Disabled perspective toggle, plus a semantic <table>/<thead>/<th scope> structure, better matching the 5-minute triage job; B relies on sort order and a single staleness checkbox with no equivalent glanceable summary. 3. At 390px, A collapses row actions into a primary "View details" button plus a "..." overflow menu (touch-friendly), while B keeps four small inline text buttons (View/Notify/Disable/Delete) per row, which is more cramped. B does have one genuine advantage worth noting: its bulk-disable confirmation explicitly warns when selected records include production connections with unrecorded production-critical status — a safeguard directly tied to the brief's stated consequence that A's provided evidence does not demonstrate at the bulk-action step (A only shows scope/count details in that dialog, with production-critical warnings only demonstrated in the single-record detail drawer).
suspected_unblinding: Packet A's source/README.md includes the line: "Design record: `.assessed/admin-connections/{PRODUCT,FRAME,STRUCTURE,CONTRACT,REVIEW-PACKET,REVIEW.json,DESIGN}.md`". This names a specific multi-stage artifact pipeline (PRODUCT/FRAME/STRUCTURE/CONTRACT/REVIEW-PACKET/DESIGN) that reads like an internal structured-design-tool convention rather than generic app documentation, which could hint that label A used a structured design process. Not acted on in scoring.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The connections table shows only a scope count badge (e.g. "3 SCOPES", "1 SCOPE") per row rather than the scope names themselves; the actual scope chips (e.g. contacts.read, deals.write) only appear after opening the record detail drawer (see A/evidence/interaction-02-inspect-one-record.png vs A/desktop.png). The brief requires a way to "inspect usage and scope before action" — B shows scope chips inline for every row without an extra click, so A adds friction to the exact judgment call (which scopes does this stale connection actually hold) the job depends on. Fix: render the real scope chips inline in the table row, at least for NEEDS REVIEW rows, instead of collapsing to a count.

findings.label: A
findings.description: The persistent selection toolbar shows only a bare count ("1 selected", "2 selected" — see A/evidence/state-02-selection-persists-across-pagination.png and interaction-03) with no indication of how many selected records are production vs sandbox; that breakdown only appears once the bulk-disable confirmation dialog is opened. B's equivalent toolbar states "2 selected · 2 production" immediately (B/evidence/state-02...png), giving the administrator a production-risk signal before committing to open the dialog. Fix: add a production-count indicator to the persistent selection bar.

findings.label: B
findings.description: B's modal dialogs (delete confirm, bulk-disable confirm, bulk-disable result, record detail) are implemented with role="dialog" but no aria-modal attribute anywhere in B/source/admin/connections/app.js, and the source contains only a single el.focus() call in the entire file with no evidence of a Tab/Shift+Tab focus trap or focus restoration on close. On a screen whose entire purpose is confirming destructive/high-consequence actions (disable, delete), a keyboard or screen-reader user could tab out of an open confirmation dialog into background rows and act on the wrong record, or a screen reader may not announce the dialog as modal at all. A, by contrast, sets aria-modal="true" on its dialogs and implements explicit first/last-element focus cycling. Fix: add aria-modal="true" to all dialog containers, implement a Tab-cycling focus trap, and restore focus to the triggering element on close.

findings.label: B
findings.description: At the required 390px viewport, B's row actions remain four separate inline text buttons (View, Notify, Disable, Delete) stacked at small size within the narrow card (B/evidence/state-04-390-px-viewport.png), which is cramped for touch targets on a real device. A instead collapses to a single primary "View details" button plus a "..." overflow control per row (A/evidence/state-04-390-px-viewport.png), which is more touch-friendly. Fix: collapse secondary actions (Notify/Delete) into an overflow menu below a viewport breakpoint, keeping only View/Disable as direct-tap primary actions.
